messages:
maria.support: heads-up — ACME (acct acme-enterprise) reporting 500s + data residency alert after what looked like a failover to us-central1. customer says they selected eu-west1 and saw requests routed elsewhere. attaching excerpt from their logs below.

sam_acme: FYI from customer: "Started seeing 500s ~2026-03-15T22:14:02Z. Trace id e7a9c1.. shows X-Region: eu-west1 in request but response headers X-Served-Region: us-central1. Also billing spike on token usage."

maria.support: reproduced locally following their repro steps — short POST to /v1/generate with region=eu-west1 header, got 500 and policy exception in audit logs.

residency-alert-bot: POLICY_EXCEPTION: cross_region_failover detected for customer=acme-enterprise request_id=e7a9c1 timestamp=2026-03-15T22:14:03Z affected_route=/v1/generate rule=eu-residency-strict action=fallback_to_compatible_region

raj.oncall: logs? give me the request_id and exact error body.

maria.support: request_id=e7a9c1, error body: "UpstreamError: incompatible-region-fallback blocked by residency policy". Full server log: 
```
ERROR 2026-03-15T22:14:03Z request=e7a9c1 routing: attempted fallback to us-central1 -> rejected by residency policy; audit: flag cross_region_failover
stack: router->policy->reject
```

alem.sre: interesting — router attempted fallback automatically (config uses fallback=true). Policy should have prevented fallback for customers with residency=eu-only. Looks like policy evaluation happened after routing decision? that's wrong ordering.

jen.product: if the policy is evaluated after routing, risk of metadata leaking or billing counting in wrong region. Legal flagged this as a compliance incident. We need containment + root cause.

ops-esc: Initial action: disable automatic fallback for all customers with residency policy set to strict. Can someone flip the flag? @raj.oncall can do a hotfix?

raj.oncall: on it. Patching router config to respect residency policy pre-routing. Will push a guarded config change: 
```
PATCH /config/router
- fallback_order: [regional_pool, global_pool]
+ fallback_order: [policy_check, regional_pool, global_pool]
```
Applying to prod-router group-2 now.

billing-bot: BILLING_ALERT: unusual token billing increase detected for acme-enterprise between 2026-03-15T22:00 and 2026-03-15T23:00 (+4200 tokens, +$12). invoice: provisional.

maria.support: customer also reports auth errors 401 on some retries — might be retry logic hitting different token issuer or short-lived credential scoped to eu region. stacktrace snippet from their client: 
```
HTTP 401 on retry attempt 2; header X-Auth-Provider: eu-kms; next attempt X-Auth-Provider: us-kms
```

alem.sre: that supports hypothesis: routing to different region caused client to hit different KMS/issuer and fail auth. We need to check token introspection logs.

raj.oncall: token-introspect shows token issuer eu-oidc returned ok for requests that stayed eu-west1; for routed->us-central1 we see issuer mismatch error: 
```
introspect request_id=e7a9c1 -> error: token_scope_mismatch (expected eu, got global)
```

ops-esc: escalation path: 1) contain (disable fallback), 2) roll-forward router config patch, 3) notify legal/compliance + customer, 4) open postmortem. Assign owners?

maria.support: I'll own customer comms and quick remediation steps. Telling ACME to pin region in their account as temporary measure.

jen.product: I'll escalate to Legal + Compliance for potential data residency breach. Need audit timeline and list of affected request_ids.

alem.sre: I'll gather router traces and confirm whether the policy check was delayed due to recent config deploy (deploy id: deploy-2026-03-15-21:40). If so, that deploy might have introduced the ordering bug.

raj.oncall: patch applied to 3/4 routers; remaining router group needs manual restart due to legacy container. Scheduling restart 22:35Z.

residency-alert-bot: FOLLOWUP: 14 requests matched cross_region_failover rule for acme-enterprise between 2026-03-15T22:12:50Z and 2026-03-15T22:15:10Z. sample_request_ids=[e7a9c1,e7a9c7,e7a9cf,...]

billing-bot: NOTE: provisional refund possible for acme-enterprise for tokens billed in non-eu regions while residency=eu-only. Finance notified.

maria.support: customer asked for reproducible steps. Repro: 
1) create api key scoped to region eu-west1
2) send POST /v1/generate with header X-Region: eu-west1 and small prompt
3) watch for 500 + residency alert in audit logs.

sam_acme: confirming we can reproduce from our side; we've saved request ids and are waiting for your remediation. We need assurance data didn't leave eu storage.

alem.sre: quick forensic note: model inferences were queued but processing attempted in us-central1 — no object storage access cross-region observed in the traces (models and KV-cache attempts were region-local), but metadata about request routing is in us-central1 logs. We need to hand off to Compliance for final determination.

jen.product: legal/compliance (cc: @legal) — please advise what evidence you need. We have router traces, audit policy exceptions, list of affected request_ids and timestamps, and token introspection logs.

ops-esc: next steps + owners: maria.support -> customer comms + confirmation; raj.oncall -> finish router rollout + verify no more fallbacks; alem.sre -> gather traces & confirm deploy timeline; jen.product -> legal liaison; billing-bot/finance -> provisional refund. I'll open an incident and link this thread.

maria.support: sent initial customer update: apologized, described immediate mitigations (disabled fallback, patching router), offered provisional refund and timeline for full postmortem. Customer acknowledged, awaiting legal confirmation. :white_check_mark:

raj.oncall: router restart done for remaining group at 22:38Z. Monitoring for repeat events.

residency-alert-bot: RESOLVED? No new cross_region_failover alerts for acme-enterprise in last 40m.

alem.sre: confirming deploy-2026-03-15-21:40 introduced a conditional reorder in router config that accidentally moved policy check after fallback selection for legacy containers. Patch PR#4112 created, will be merged to main after code review.

jen.product: legal requested packaged evidence by 2026-03-16 09:00 local. Alems and Raj, please attach traces + audit export to the incident ticket.

ops-esc: incident ticket INC-2026-232 opened, linking this thread and owners. We'll do a public postmortem if legal confirms a breach.

maria.support: closing loop with customer: they accepted provisional refund and asked for prep instructions for region pinning. Sent step-by-step.

sam_acme: thanks team — appreciate the quick response. Please keep us posted.

maria.support: summary: cause = router deploy reordered policy check -> allowed fallback -> cross-region routing triggered token mismatch and 500s for acme-enterprise. mitigation = disabled fallback + router patch + restart + refund offer. owners assigned, postmortem planned.

ops-esc: marking this thread for follow-up in the postmortem doc. If anything new pops up, @ops-esc here. :spiral_note_pad:
